about: Week 1 is short, Tuesday to Sunday, so it is deliberately light on content and heavy on getting set up. Do the setup first. It takes an hour and it saves you from finding out in Week 6 that something does not work.
watch: The difference between *homeostasis* and *equilibrium*. They are not the same thing and the distinction shows up on every exam in this course.
The seven parts of a feedback loop. Learn them once here and you will recognize them in every system for the rest of the term.
*Osmolarity counts particles*, not molecules. This one sentence will save you in Week 3.
A number without a unit is not an answer. Start that habit now.
knowlead: Week 1 is mostly concepts rather than structures, so this list is short. It gets longer from Week 3 on.

chapters.title: Introduction to Physiology
chapters.note: The whole chapter. It is short and it sets up the vocabulary.

chapters.title: Communication, Integration, and Homeostasis
chapters.note: Read the homeostasis, feedback loop and control pathway sections only. The cell signaling half of this chapter comes back in Week 4, so leave it.

steps.title: Start Here, and the tech check
steps.do: Work through the entry page. It checks that your browser, camera and uploads all work, and it takes about fifteen minutes. Do it before anything else, because everything later assumes it passed.

steps.title: Read the syllabus and take the syllabus quiz
steps.do: The quiz is open book and you can retake it. It exists so that nobody reaches Week 6 not knowing how the course works.

steps.title: Introduce yourself
steps.do: Post your vision board and a short video introducing yourself. Completion based, ten points, no wrong answers.

steps.title: Meet your patient
steps.do: You are assigned one patient for the whole term and nobody else has yours. Open their file, read it, and keep it somewhere you can find it every week.

steps.title: Watch the Week 1 video
steps.do: About forty minutes. Watch it before the reading, not after: it tells you what to look for.

steps.title: Read Silverthorn Ch 1 and the homeostasis half of Ch 6
steps.do: Read with the *what to watch for* list above next to you. You are reading for the pattern, not for every detail.

steps.title: Work the practice questions
steps.do: Keep going until you can get them right with nothing open. Every wrong answer tells you why it is wrong, so read those even when you guessed correctly.

steps.title: Do the problem set
steps.do: Solve them by hand first, cite where you found what you needed, then check with AI. The log walks you through it and the first two boxes are the ones I grade.

steps.title: Patient chart entry
steps.do: Draw the feedback loop from memory with the book closed, applied to your patient. Note what you left out. Then open the book and correct it *in a different color*. A wrong drawing that you caught is a perfect entry.
steps.where: Paper or the drawing canvas, submit in Canvas

steps.title: Weekly post
steps.do: One post, two halves. Something from this week's physiology in your own words, and the gap you found in your own retrieval plus what you are going to do about it.

nextline: Chemistry, and only the chemistry that actually does work in the body. Lighter than this week looks.
oneline: The week the whole course is built on. Everything later is a variation on what is here: something held steady, something measuring it, something correcting it.
